question_en:
A hedge fund manager is estimating a value for a non-traded bond of Yoder Company. The bond has an annual-pay 6% coupon, matures in six years, and has a CCC credit rating. Actively traded annual-pay bonds with similar credit ratings include the following:

| Coupon | Maturity | Yield to maturity |
|---|---|---|
| 8% | 5 years | 9.45% |
| 5% | 5 years | 9.55% |
| 7% | 10 years | 10.00% |

Based on matrix pricing, the value of the Yoder bond as a percentage of par is closest to:
explanation_en: To find an appropriate discount rate for the Yoder bond, first take the average of the 5-year bonds: (9.45% + 9.55%) / 2 = 9.50% Next, use linear interpolation to estimate a yield for a bond with six years to maturity: 9.50% + [(6 − 5) / (10 − 5)] × (10.00% − 9.50%) = 9.60% Finally, discount the Yoder bond's cash flows at this rate: N = 6; I/Y = 9.6; PMT = 6; FV = 100; CPT PV = –84.14

question_en: For a stock that has a beta of 0.95, it is most likely that:
option_a: the slope of its characteristic line is 0.95.
option_b: the market is 95% as volatile as this individual stock.
option_c: the variance of the market return is 95% of the covariance of the stock’s return with the market return.
explanation_en: The slope of a security's characteristic line is its beta. This stock is 95% as volatile as the market, and the covariance of its return with the market return is 95% of the variance of the market return.

question_en: An analyst is most likely to examine a company's channel strategy when evaluating the company's:
explanation_en: Evaluating a company's business model includes examining its channel strategy, which refers to the means by which a company sells its products or services (e.g., directly to customers or through intermediaries). Revenue drivers include top-down factors such as economic growth and bottom-up factors such as business segments or geography. Pricing power depends on an industry's structure and degree of competition.

question_en: In the context of risk management, entering an interest rate swap is an example of:
explanation_en: When organizations decide to reduce or eliminate a risk, they may use risk shifting (e.g., buying forwards, futures, or swaps) or risk transfers (e.g., buy insurance). When organizations decide to bear a risk, they may use diversification to help them bear risk more efficiently.

question_en: A 7.5% coupon, semiannual-pay, five-year bond has a yield to maturity of 6.80%. Over the next year, if the bond's yield to maturity remains unchanged, its price will:
explanation_en: Because the coupon rate is greater than its yield to maturity, the bond price is at a premium to par value. If the yield remains unchanged, the price will decrease toward par value along its constant-yield price trajectory.

question_en: Co-investing is most accurately described as investing:
option_a: as a limited partner in an investment fund, but only committing capital to one or more of the fund’s portfolio companies.
option_b: directly in one or more of an investment fund’s portfolio companies, instead of investing as a limited partner in the fund.
option_c: directly in one or more of an investment fund’s portfolio companies, in addition to investing as a limited partner in the fund.
explanation_en: Co-investing refers to investing in a fund as a limited partner, while additionally investing directly in some of the assets in which the fund invests.

question_en: A securities market exhibits operational efficiency if it offers:
option_b: prices that respond rapidly to new information.
option_c: rates of return that are proportional to risk on average.
explanation_en: Operational efficiency refers to low transactions costs in a securities market. Informational efficiency means prices change rapidly to reflect new information without predictable bias and rates of return are, on average, proportional to risk.

question_en: Other things equal, the value of a long position in a forward contract priced at F(0)T will most likely be higher during its life at time t if the:
option_b: costs of holding the underlying are lower.
option_c: benefits of holding the underlying are higher.
explanation_en: During its life value of a forward contract is: [St + PVt (costs of holding) – PVt (benefits of holding)] – F(0)T × (1 + Rf)–(T – t). A higher risk-free rate will increase the value of a long forward position during its life. Lower costs or higher benefits from holding the underlying will decrease the value of a long forward position.

question_en: The type of credit risk that is most directly reflected in a bond's rating is:
explanation_en: Default risk is the possibility that the issuer will fail to meet its obligations under the indenture, for which investors demand a premium above the return on a default- risk-free security. Bond ratings indicate default risk. Downgrade risk is the risk that a bond will be reclassified as a riskier security by a credit rating agency. Credit spread risk is the risk that the default risk premium on a bond can increase.

question_en: Portfolio duration most accurately approximates the sensitivity of the value of a bond portfolio to:
option_a: parallel shifts in the yield curve.
option_b: increases in the slope of the yield curve.
option_c: decreases in the slope of the yield curve.
explanation_en: Portfolio duration is an approximation of the price sensitivity of a portfolio to parallel shifts of the yield curve (yields for all maturities increase or decrease by equal amounts). Key rate duration may be used to estimate interest rate risk for non-parallel shifts in the yield curve.

question_en: Open-end mutual funds differ from closed-end funds in that:
option_a: open-end funds stand ready to redeem their shares, while closed-end funds do not.
option_b: closed-end funds require active management, while open-end funds do not.
option_c: open-end funds issue shares that are then traded in secondary markets, while closed-end funds do not.
explanation_en: Open-end funds redeem existing shares or issue new shares in accordance with investor demand. Closed-end fund shares are fixed in number and trade on exchanges as though they were common stock.

question_en: During the life of an option, the amount by which its price is greater than its exercise value is most accurately described as its:
explanation_en: Before expiration, an option can have a price greater than its exercise or intrinsic value. This amount by which an option's price is greater than its exercise value is referred to as its time value.

question_en: An investor purchases 1,000 shares of each of the stocks in a price-weighted index at their closing prices (ignore transactions costs). On a total return basis, if the index stocks remain the same, this portfolio will most likely:
option_a: perform exactly like the index over time.
explanation_en: Total return includes dividend yield. Because dividends are not included in the performance of the index itself, the portfolio will outperform the index by the amount of the dividend yield.
